Statement of the problem: A bus terminal is to be constructed on a 5,400 sqm rectangular inside lot in Pasay City. The lot is facing south and slopes 2% towards a 40 m RROW. The lot frontage is 60 m. It will serve 17–25 buses at any given time and has a waiting area (20 m x 16 m) that can accommodate 150 persons, rentable lockers (15 m x 15 m), a bus maintenance repair shed (20 m x 25 m) at the rear northwest corner, a restaurant (18 m x 10 m), a food court (18 m x 18 m), and open-air bus parking (60 m x 50 m). There is an abutting firewall on the west side near the front.

q: What is the FLAR maximum of the Project?
n: Utility/Transportation/RROW/Services has an FLAR of 2.00 up to 3.00, so the maximum is 3.00. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VII, Table VII.G.1.

scenario:
PROPOSED PARKING BUILDING PROJECT

Statement of the problem: A three-storey parking building will be erected on a 5,350 sqm rectangular inside lot in Pasig City. The lot is facing south, slopes 3% towards a 12 m RROW, and has a depth of 50 m. Each floor can accommodate 150 cars. The building footprint is 70 m x 36 m. The ramps are located 20 m from both sides.

q: What is the actual PSO of the project?
n: PSO = 2,520 / 5,350 = 47.1%, or about 47%. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VIII, Sec. 803.

n: A parking building is a Utility/Transportation/Services use. Without firewall, the maximum ISA is 40%. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VIII, Table VIII.1.

q: Under Rule VII of the Revised IRR of the 1977 NBCP, what is meant by PSO?
n: PSO stands for Percentage of Site Occupancy. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VII and Rule VIII, Sec. 803.

q: Under Rule VII of the Revised IRR of the 1977 NBCP, what is meant by AMBF?
n: AMBF stands for Allowable Maximum Building Footprint. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VII, Table VII.1.

q: Which is NOT part of Architectural Interiors (AI)?
n: Eaves are part of the exterior roof assembly, not of the architectural interiors (ceilings, partitions, interior floor finishes). Source: RA 9266 IRR, Sec. 3 (Definition of Architectural Interiors); UAP Doc. 208 (Architectural Interiors).

q: Which is NOT considered a fixture?
n: A fixture is fastened to the building and served by its utilities (fans, luminaires, toilet accessories). A wall hanging is loose decor and not a fixture. Source: Ching, Interior Design Illustrated (Furnishings vs. Fixtures); Harris, Dictionary of Architecture and Construction.
